objectReviews.sourceCompleteness: Both versions retain induction and the magnetic properties of matter, distinguish the previously emphasized static cases from time-varying fields, and keep the importance of further alternating/high-frequency study. The dated ninth-grade time-limit statement and unsupported superlatives are replaced without dropping a scientific topic.

checks.assessment: Both versions describe electrostatic fields from stationary charges in the implied study frame. Neither claims that charge motion must be absent in all microscopic processes or that electrostatics exhausts electrodynamics.

Both versions correctly identify time-independent magnetic fields from steady currents or stable magnetic sources. Moving current carriers are compatible with a steady macroscopic current distribution; an isolated charge's constant velocity does not by itself make its field time-independent at a fixed observation point. The explicit third sentence removes the original shortcut rather than repeating it.
checks.enAnchor: a magnetostatic field is defined by not changing with time

checks.assessment: The induction statement is a description of the preceding learning progression, not a claim that every possible induction experiment requires a locally changing magnetic field. Neither language excludes motional induction. Further alternating/high-frequency phenomena are presented as important, not as the only important electromagnetic phenomena.

objectReviews.bilingualAgreement: The Chinese five complete sentences and their English counterparts agree on static-source conditions, moving carriers, time independence, the role of induction and the remaining study topics. Different paragraph spacing does not change scientific meaning.

objectReviews.sourceCompleteness: Both versions retain the full roadmap: previously learned electrodynamic laws; AC properties, generation and applications; time-varying electric fields and magnetic fields; high-frequency fields and electromagnetic waves; and a broader understanding of electromagnetic processes.

checks.assessment: The text distinguishes a changing magnetic field inducing an electric field from the magnetic-field contribution associated with a time-varying electric field. The latter is the Maxwell-Ampere displacement-current contribution, not Faraday induction run backward, not a reversal of induced-current direction and not a need for conducting charges at the observation point. Both versions use correspondence rather than the original literal inverse-phenomenon label.
checks.enAnchor: a time-varying electric field can also produce a magnetic field

checks.assessment: The necessary time dependence appears explicitly in both languages; neither substitutes a static electric field, omits the condition, asserts instantaneous action or claims that a pointwise nonzero electric-field derivative alone determines the local magnetic-field value. Equations and a derivation are appropriately left to the later substantive lesson.

Building from known laws to AC, then the complementary time-varying-field relation and finally electromagnetic waves is coherent. It is a suggested study sequence rather than a universal curricular schedule. The conclusion does not equate AC with high frequency or claim that all electromagnetic waves are high-frequency.

Both learner texts remove tenth-grade and next-year predictions. Further development/more complete understanding agrees with the Chinese further improvement/more comprehensive understanding; neither promises mastery of all electrodynamics or the entire electromagnetic process of nature.

objectReviews.bilingualAgreement: All four statements match conceptually: prior laws as foundation; AC properties/generation/uses; time-dependent E-to-B in correspondence with changing-B-to-induced-E; high-frequency fields and waves; and a broader rather than exhaustive understanding. English 'We will also explore' carries no dated grade/year prediction and does not change the scientific conditions.
